candidateReviewSemantics: Complete table of every serious card candidate considered after testing all 13 definitions; accepted and rejected decisions are both preserved.

candidateReviews.label: Equivocation
candidateReviews.rationale: Aron Ra treats “substance” as necessarily material when declaring “immaterial substance” contradictory, without addressing Hernandez’s metaphysical use of the term.
candidateReviews.context: He calls “immaterial substance” self-contradictory by treating substance as material rather than addressing Hernandez’s metaphysical meaning.

candidateReviews.label: Scope neglect
candidateReviews.rationale: The categorical claim that spiritual revelations never exceed prior belief expands culturally familiar examples to the entire class without proportional evidential support.
candidateReviews.context: He generalizes from culturally familiar visions to the absolute claim that spiritual revelations never contain previously unknown material.

candidateReviews.label: Appeal to authority
candidateReviews.rationale: Dennett and Churchland are invoked as support for brain-generated consciousness, but their status substitutes for the missing explanation of how neural activity produces the disputed mental properties.
candidateReviews.context: He invokes Dennett and Churchland’s description of consciousness as neuronal activity instead of supplying the disputed explanatory bridge.

candidateReviews.label: Authority bias
candidateReviews.rationale: Although named authorities receive argumentative weight, the excerpt does not establish the speaker’s private tendency to overweight authority beyond the visible appeal-to-authority defect.

candidateReviews.label: Begging the question
candidateReviews.rationale: The opening physical-object-or-soul dichotomy assumes the exhaustive ontological alternatives needed to infer a soul, thereby embedding the disputed conclusion in the setup.
candidateReviews.context: He begins with “either a purely physical object or an immaterial soul,” assuming the exhaustive alternatives needed for his conclusion.

candidateReviews.label: Equivocation
candidateReviews.rationale: “Divided” shifts from the partition of physical components to possessing personhood in percentages, so two different senses drive the nonidentity inference.
candidateReviews.context: He shifts from physical objects being divisible into parts to personhood not occurring in percentages or degrees.

candidateReviews.label: Begging the question
candidateReviews.rationale: The physical-object-or-soul premise presupposes the exhaustive contrast required for the conclusion, excluding organized physical continuity at the outset rather than defeating it.
candidateReviews.context: He assumes one must be either a purely physical object lacking persistence or an immaterial soul before arguing for the soul.

candidateReviews.label: Begging the question
candidateReviews.rationale: The body-transfer example asserts that the transferred mind would no longer be the person, even though that identity discontinuity is the point the example must establish.
candidateReviews.context: He says a mind placed in another body would no longer be you, assuming the disputed identity discontinuity.

candidateReviews.label: Subjective validation
candidateReviews.rationale: The reply draws partly on introspection, but it does not treat a claim as accurate merely because it personally resonates; it advances a general distinction between causal influence and rational incapacity.

candidateReviews.label: Subjective validation
candidateReviews.rationale: The speaker references his experience of information-sensitive choice, but the assessment identifies an incomplete metaphysical inference rather than reliance on personal resonance as validation.

candidateReviews.label: Equivocation
candidateReviews.rationale: Aron Ra shifts Hernandez’s “animates” from a consciousness-bearing soul’s relation to the body to vitalism’s biological life force, then treats refuting the latter as answering the former.
candidateReviews.context: He recasts the soul’s proposed animation of the body as vitalism’s obsolete biological life force.

candidateReviews.label: Argument from ignorance
candidateReviews.rationale: Hernandez imposes an excessive burden on physicalism, but this excerpt does not explicitly treat the soul as true merely because complete mind-brain identity has not been proved.

candidateReviews.label: Appeal to authority
candidateReviews.rationale: Doctors, reputable people, and journals are mentioned vaguely, but Hernandez expressly declines to present the reports as a defended argument; the citation does not function as settling proof.

candidateReviews.label: Appeal to authority
candidateReviews.rationale: Calling a paper peer-reviewed is a citation-quality claim, but Aron Ra also alleges conflicting findings and reproduced effects rather than treating publication status alone as decisive.

candidateReviews.label: Scope neglect
candidateReviews.rationale: The claim that the God helmet duplicates “all” relevant effects fails to scale the conclusion to the narrow, unspecified effects actually described.
candidateReviews.context: He says the God helmet duplicates all out-of-body effects without distinguishing the range or frequency of experiences reproduced.

candidateReviews.label: Scope neglect
candidateReviews.rationale: Evidence that physical stimulation produces some deceptive impressions is expanded into the categorical judgment that the experiences are entirely physical, disregarding the class’s broader scope.
candidateReviews.context: He moves from some brain-induced impressions to calling sensed presences and out-of-body experiences entirely physical.

overallCandidateReviews.label: Begging the question
overallCandidateReviews.rationale: The physical-object-or-soul choice assumes the exhaustive ontological alternatives required to reach the soul conclusion, rather than independently establishing them.

overallCandidateReviews.label: Equivocation
overallCandidateReviews.rationale: The argument moves between physical components being divisible and personhood admitting degrees, using different senses of divisibility as though they were one property.

overallCandidateReviews.label: Equivocation
overallCandidateReviews.rationale: Calling “immaterial substance” contradictory relies on a material sense of substance while failing to address the metaphysical bearer Hernandez intended.

overallCandidateReviews.label: Appeal to authority
overallCandidateReviews.rationale: The neuronal-generation reply relies on cited theorists’ conclusion while leaving their relevant evidence and the mechanism answering Hernandez’s mental-property arguments undeveloped.

overallCandidateReviews.label: Scope neglect
overallCandidateReviews.rationale: Absolute claims about cultural expectation, report inconsistency, and duplicated effects extend limited and poorly documented observations across the broader class of paranormal reports.
